summary: SL-104 widened the settled Fitness rules from SL-056 (rule 2, the timestamp/attribute writer fence, and rule 4, the directory-listing fence) in .taad/fitness.yaml. Rule 2 now has 11 patterns and rule 4 has 7. It also added one engine-appended Attributes-setter entry (70 settled entries now), 25 plant rows (S58-S82), a 178-row class corpus with a runner, and rewritten because-texts. The acceptance repro goes from exit 1 to exit 0, the 161-row harness is fully AS-RECORDED, and src is byte-identical. Four more spelling families that code review found were waived to the backlog (SC-321, SC-322, SC-323, plus SC-320 for harness-case grouping). The rules therefore still do not fence every spelling their corpus claims to bound.

payload.estimate_error: Opened as medium size and medium risk, sized by a person. Size was under-called: the design said the repro was the only new test and expected yaml lines plus 21 plant rows, but the build changed 9 files. Accepted class_of findings (M1, M2) forced a committed 178-row corpus plus a runner with a live .NET 10 census, and gate load was two critiques and two code reviews. Risk was over-called: no product code changed, the build passed on its first attempt, and all 5 spikes held. The loop was in the gates, not in the build.

lessons_judged.why: The design kept spike 1's full sibling-family union instead of the 2-line R2-m4 minimum, explicitly citing this lesson. It was incomplete on the syntax axis, though: ++/--, deconstruction, using-alias method groups and whitespace/@ after the dot all escaped later.

Its content is about \\?\ path spellings, which did not bear here. Its general principle, to run a critique-proposed regex against a corpus before the builder gets it, was not followed for M2's receiver-free \.(Encrypt|Decrypt)\b. Validate then measured it firing on rsa.Encrypt(...).

It says the build must move engine-appended rules above the first '# settled by' marker and add an xUnit Fact and including_comments. SL-104 left the Attributes entry at file end under a single SL-104 marker, with no twin. rules-parity stayed AGREE (70 settled not compared), and RuleCases and the harness passed. The move-and-twin step applies only when the design chooses a twin.
The design read fitness.yaml and rules-parity first and declared rules 2 and 4 and the Attributes entry settled with no twin. Parity moved only the settled count, 69 to 70.
ArchitectureRulesTests.cs was not edited, so its closed grammar never came into play.

The accepted M6 split the guard into rules-parity plus one RuleCases -Case per command. The build ran C-001..C-005 one at a time and C-001 passed under the engine TEMP. The quoted counts in the lesson are stale: parity now reads 18 facts <- 22 twinned, 48 patterns, 70 settled.

The design cited #400 and #439 to decline widening further and to file the AST/symbol route for later. Four more spelling families surfaced after the build, which is evidence that route is now due. The rule-C counts it quotes were not touched.

It says any rule edit must change both fitness.yaml and ArchitectureRulesTests.cs, and that there are 8 entries. SL-104 edited two existing settled entries and added one, in yaml only, against a 92-rule file with 22 twinned entries, and parity stayed AGREE.
Plant S64 sits directly under src/FsAnalyser.Core to prove ** reaches zero levels. A settled entry without including_comments matches code only, which shaped the plant and because-text wording.

It bore on this slice but did not change what was done. The design still said the repro was the only new test, and the build grew to 9 files with a corpus and runner. That repeats the 'one Fact' undercount pattern.

The harness command form with --engine-root and the .dotnet SDK 10.0.401 requirement were followed. The 32-row matrix it quotes is stale: the all scenario is now 161 rows, 148 in plants.json, 92 rules in the clean baseline.
Every build and test ran through eng/dotnet.ps1. The survey's first run installed SDK 10.0.401 into the worktree's gitignored .dotnet/, as the lesson predicts.

learned.lesson: Fencing the whole API family (#225) is not enough for a text rule in .taad/fitness.yaml. It also needs a checklist of syntactic spellings of each member. The slice missed these: ++/-- on the Attributes enum property, deconstruction assignment, a method group through a using alias, whitespace/newline/comment/@ between the dot and the member, object initializers, reflection. Hand the designer and critic this list for any 'every way to X is fenced' rule: call, method group, using static, using alias, fully qualified, op= (+= -= |= &= ^=), ++/--, deconstruction, initializer, @identifier, spacing around the dot.
learned.evidence: Code review round 1 found ++/-- and deconstruction (m1) and the alias method group (m2). Round 2 found the dot-to-name gap (R2-n1). Spikes and the critique found none of the four. SC-321, SC-322 and SC-323 were waived to the backlog.

learned.lesson: On a rule-widening slice, an accepted finding with a class_of makes the engine require a committed corpus and runner with mutation proof. Plan that at design time. The design said the repro was the only new test, but the build added tests/bugs/SL-104-SettledRuleClassCorpus.json (178 rows, 40 census members) and its runner. Size such slices medium or larger even when src is untouched. The corpus's 'bounded_by' wording is itself a claim that code review checks, so write it narrowly.
learned.evidence: build-slice #1 lists the corpus and runner as a declared deviation (O-017, O-018). The corpus claimed 'each operator the property type defines' and 'every spelling the compiler accepts', and code review contradicted both.

learned.lesson: A receiver-free pattern on a common verb (Encrypt, Decrypt, GetFiles, Attributes) needs quiet rows for non-file receivers. The corpus's 41 quiet rows contained no RSA/crypto look-alike, so M2's `\.(Encrypt|Decrypt)\b` over-fenced undetected until validate.
learned.evidence: Validate case X1: `var c = rsa.Encrypt(data, RSAEncryptionPadding.OaepSHA256);` fired rule 2. The build, corpus runner and harness all passed with the pattern in place.

learned.lesson: SC-321, SC-322 and SC-323 edit the same few pattern lines and the same corpus. Bundle them with the Encrypt narrowing into one slice rather than three. Each separate slice would repay the harness (161 rows) and the 178-row corpus runner. All three fixes are small: `\.` becomes `\.\s*@?`, the SetAttributes/Set*Time patterns become receiver-free, and the Attributes pattern gains `|\+\+|--`.
learned.evidence: Waived O-024, O-025 and O-026 touch rule 2 (.taad/fitness.yaml:753-759), rule 4 (:793) and the Attributes entry (:1254) as quoted in the findings. None adds a pattern line.

learned.lesson: For rule-text slices, a second code-review round framed as an attacker is worth it. Round 2 on the same diff found a gap round 1 missed (R2-n1). But every late minor was model-disposed and then waived to the backlog, so the loop ended with its own class claim still false. If a minor is a zero-line pattern edit and the harness and corpus are already built, say so in the finding. A waive is cheap to accept and expensive to repay later.
learned.evidence: Code review ran 2 rounds: 2 findings in round 1, 1 in round 2, all 3 waived. The edit sizes are in O-024, O-025 and O-026. The 10 critique and review dispositions were model-answered and counted as untriaged.

learned.lesson: The critique's m1 premise, that many harness --only cases would cost ~11x and hit the 120 s case kill (Q-222), did not hold for this tree. The full 161-row harness through the real engine took 26 s, and each case command ran standalone in 14-18 s. SC-320 (grouping the harness cases) is worth only the saved build time, not the kill risk. Treat it as low value when the backlog is swept.
learned.evidence: build-slice #1: 'harness.py ... --scenario all' 26 s, 161/161 AS-RECORDED. Each case command exited 0 in 14-18 s. Code review's rerun of the full scenario was also 26 s.

learned.lesson: A critique disposition must not promise an edit to a record another stage owns. M4's disposition said the design's architecture_rules entry would be updated to the M1 pattern, but only the design stage writes design-slice-1.json. The build edited the yaml block in place and code review logged drift. Either route such a change back to design, or write 'stale record is harmless because design.py only appends unseen names'.
learned.evidence: Code review drift: design-slice-1.json still holds `(?m)\.Attributes\s*[|&^]?=(?!=)`; the tree holds `[-+|&^]?=(?![=>])`. The builder declared it.

learned.lesson: Risk spikes that plant lines in three places (Store/, the Core root, an unexcepted Scanning file) and run taad3.fitness.content_hits are predictive for fitness.yaml widenings. They found the (?![=>]) lookahead and the DirectoryReader.cs:181 separate-entry need, and all 5 held at build. They only test the spellings someone listed, so add the syntax checklist to the planted set.
learned.evidence: Spikes 1-5 all 'go'. Build discharged the O-015/O-016 preconditions with 0 stray hits across 161 rows. The four late gaps were spellings no spike planted.

what_went_wrong: The slice shipped with its own class claim still false. The corpus says it bounds 'every spelling the compiler accepts', yet ++/-- on Attributes, deconstruction, a using-alias method group and whitespace/@ after the dot all compile and escape every pattern. All four were found only by code review, so the O-031 failure mode (a rule claiming more than it fences) survives in a narrower form. The five escape spellings from the earlier waivers are on the backlog as SC-321, SC-322 and SC-323.

The design said the repro was the only new test and pinned 21 plant rows and a `_note` count of 144. The build delivered 25 rows, 148 in plants.json, and a 178-row corpus with a runner (9 files). All of it was declared, but the design's size claim was off by a whole test subsystem.

Critique and code review each ran twice. Both first runs halted on findings waiting for disposition, and every disposition (7 critique, 3 code review) was model-answered and counted as untriaged. No person has checked any of them, so these gates' precision is still unmeasured.

The critique's own fix for M2, the receiver-free `\.(Encrypt|Decrypt)\b`, over-fences non-file receivers. Validate found `rsa.Encrypt(...)` firing rule 2. The proposed regex was not run against a quiet-corpus before the build, and the 41 quiet corpus rows did not cover it.

M4's disposition promised to update design-slice-1.json, which the build cannot do. The design record still carries the pre-M1 Attributes pattern and the old because-text. Harmless while the yaml block exists, but a stale pattern would come back if the block were ever deleted and the design re-run.

Validate marked the acceptance repro (SL-104-SettledRuleSpellings.Tests.ps1) not-run, along with the whole xUnit suite, RuleCases C-002..C-005 and the minorlane merge gate. It substituted its own 46-case matrix, and the build and code review had run the repro. The acceptance command was discharged by the engine (O-001), but validate itself did not re-run it.

The untracked .taad-scratch/ (about 95 Planted*.cs files, copies of fitness.yaml, probe scripts) from the repro and investigation stages was still in the worktree at build. The record does not show it removed before the slice ships.

missed.what: M1 widened the setter patterns to `[-+|&^]?=` for compound assignment but did not enumerate the other assignment forms of the same properties. Unary `fi.Attributes++` / `--` (enum) and deconstruction `(fi.LastWriteTime, fi.Attributes) = (...)` both compile and match no pattern. A check could ask, for each fenced property setter, which assignment forms C# permits (=, op=, ++/--, deconstruction, initializer).
missed.caught_by: code-review round 1 (m1, O-024 waived to SC-321)

missed.what: The design made only Encrypt/Decrypt receiver-free (via M2). `\bFile\.SetAttributes\b` and `\b(File|Directory)\.Set(LastAccess|LastWrite|Creation)Time` still need the literal type name, so a method group through `using F = System.IO.File;` (`F.SetAttributes`) escapes. The inconsistency was visible in the design, since rule 4's instance pattern was already receiver-free.
missed.caught_by: code-review round 1 (m2, O-025 waived to SC-322)

missed.what: No question was asked about what C# allows between the member-access dot and the member name: spaces, a newline, a /* */ comment (blanked to spaces by strip_comments) or an `@` verbatim identifier. Every dotted pattern in rule 2, rule 4 and the Attributes entry needs the name directly after `.`. Eight such lines compiled and fired no rule under Store/.
missed.caught_by: code-review round 2 (R2-n1, O-026 waived to SC-323)

missed.what: Round 1 compiled and probed alias and deconstruction spellings against the same diff but did not probe whitespace, newline or `@` between the dot and the member. Only the second 'attacker' round found it. Any round-1 review of a text rule should try token-level spacing variants of every dotted pattern.

The M2 fix replaced `\bFile\.(Encrypt|Decrypt)\b` with the receiver-free `\.(Encrypt|Decrypt)\b` without running it against non-file receivers (RSA, other crypto types). It over-fences `rsa.Encrypt(...)`. The critique should have asked what other types in System.* expose Encrypt/Decrypt.
missed.caught_by: validate (driver case X1: `var c = rsa.Encrypt(data, RSAEncryptionPadding.OaepSHA256);` fires rule 2)

missed.what: The M4 disposition said the design's architecture_rules entry is updated to the M1 pattern. Only the design stage can write design-slice-1.json, so the build could not honour it, and the design record kept the pre-M1 pattern and because-text.
missed.caught_by: code-review round 1 (undeclared-drift line; builder had also declared it)

unknowns: Does anything re-run tests/bugs/SL-104-SettledRuleClassCorpus.Tests.ps1 after the slice merges? It is not in the default dotnet test run, and rules 2 and 4 and the Attributes entry have no xUnit twin. Only the Fitness check and the harness exercise them, so the 178-row corpus and its live .NET 10 census may be dead weight once the slice's own cases stop being measured.
Does the engine's merge-time minorlane gate behave the same on the 92-rule yaml? Validate ran fitness.check through the MCP tool and the harness, not the gate itself, so this was not reached.

Would model-answered dispositions survive a person's check? Ten findings (7 critique, 3 code review) were answered by a model and none was reviewed. Four spelling families were then waived on 'does not weigh a lap on its own'. It is unknown whether a person would have taken the zero-line pattern fixes in this slice.

candidates.title: Narrow rule 2's receiver-free Encrypt/Decrypt pattern so non-file receivers do not fire it, and add quiet rows
candidates.why: Rule 2 'only the directory-listing open path may write a file-system timestamp' in .taad/fitness.yaml carries `(?m)\.(Encrypt|Decrypt)\b` (about :759 at the SL-104 code review; the tree may have moved). Validate #128 driver case X1 `var c = rsa.Encrypt(data, RSAEncryptionPadding.OaepSHA256);` fired it. Nothing is wrong today: validate found no Core use of Encrypt/Decrypt, and the diff shows no src change. But a legitimate crypto call in Core would fail a settled rule. The 41 quiet rows in tests/bugs/SL-104-SettledRuleClassCorpus.json have no non-file receiver. Fold this into the SC-321/SC-322/SC-323 pattern pass instead of a separate slice. The backlog is at its ceiling (31 open against 30), and SL-104 is itself a one-deep follow-up, so this may not land until others are built or swept.
